description: CHAT Large Natural Areas Large Natural Areas are areas greater than 1,000 ha (2,471 ac) that are minimally fragmented by roads, powerlines, railroads, pipelines, and other human impacts. Areas were delineated using the Landscape Condition Model of Comer and Hak (2012), which computes a Landscape Condition score for 90 x 90-meter pixels based on each pixel's distance from 19 impact elements associated with transportation, urban/industrial development, and managed or modified land cover (e.g., cultivated areas). Using protected areas as a reference (USGS Protected Areas Database Gap status 1–3), a minimum Landscape Condition score threshold was determined that represents a natural area, stratified by plains, mountain, and desert ecosystems. A 1,000-ha moving-window smoothing process was then performed to identify Large Intact Blocks (LIBs) containing contiguous areas above their respective ecosystem threshold values. For each LIB, an average Landscape Condition score was computed, and LIBs were proportionally binned into three Large Natural Area classes (highest third, middle third, and lowest third in condition above the threshold). For hexagons that crossed two or more Large Natural Areas polygons, the hexagon was assigned to the class with the lowest value occupying at least 25% of the hexagon. description: CHAT Freshwater Integrity Freshwater Integrity is a measure of watershed stress from human impacts and the risk of potential degradation to aquatic habitat. It is based on the average National Fish Habitat Action Plan (NFHAP) Cumulative Disturbance value, which ranges from 1–5. Watersheds scoring 5 have the lowest stress and degradation and are of the highest value for habitat maintenance, while watersheds scoring 1 are under the highest stress and at greatest risk of degradation. Freshwater Integrity rankings are not regulatory and do not imply specific avoidance or mitigation measures. They represent the relative condition and stress level of a watershed as it pertains to aquatic habitat value. Priority Criteria 1 – Most Crucial NFHAP value = 5; very low potential watershed degradation (minimum stress; highest benefit to aquatic organisms) 2 NFHAP value = 4; low potential watershed degradation (low stress) 3 NFHAP value = 3; moderate potential watershed degradation (moderate stress) 4 NFHAP value = 2; high potential watershed degradation (high stress) 5 – Least Crucial NFHAP value = 1; very high potential watershed degradation (very high stress; lowest benefit to aquatic organisms) 6 – No Data No data available for these areas; watershed was not evaluated by NFHAP For more info visit NM-CHAT .
